job.title: Family Lawyer
job.description:
The Opportunity

This is a growing national firm with a strong Canterbury presence, focused on supporting its people to succeed in meaningful work while fostering a connected and people-focused team culture.
They are seeking a Family Lawyer based in their Christchurch office. This is a genuine opportunity to do meaningful work — helping people navigate some of the most challenging times by providing compassionate, pragmatic advice.

About the Role

You will work closely with experienced family lawyers and legal executives, supported by a dedicated PA. Under the guidance of x2 Partners, you will manage your own files, develop your advocacy and negotiation skills, appear in Court, and progressively take on more complex and higher-value matters.
Key areas of work include some or all of the following:
  • Separation and divorce
  • Care of children
  • Protection orders and family violence matters
  • Spousal maintenance
  • Relationship property and contracting-out agreements
  • PPPR applications
About You

The firm is looking for a lawyer ranging from a strong graduate through to approximately four years’ post-qualification experience in family law or a closely related area (litigation or trusts experience will also be considered). Strong graduates who demonstrate real maturity, resilience, a “get up and go” attitude, and excellent technical ability are encouraged to apply.

You will need:
  • A genuine passion for family law and a client-focused, empathetic approach
  • Solid academic and practical ability, with the maturity and wisdom to thrive in a busy practice
  • A clear understanding of billable hours and a willingness to work productively to meet targets
  • A positive outlook, strong work ethic, and the ability to work collaboratively in a supportive team environment
Previous experience in a law firm setting is preferred, but they are focused on finding the right person with a positive attitude and potential.

What's on Offer
  • A collaborative, team-first culture where your development is genuinely invested in
  • Flexible working arrangements, including support for returning parents and openness to alternative patterns for the right candidate
  • The opportunity to build a rewarding career alongside expert practitioners
  • A friendly, approachable workplace with excellent coffee and morning teas
The firm prides itself on being pragmatic, supportive, and fully committed to both outstanding client outcomes and the wellbeing of its team.

If you are a capable, empathetic, and driven family lawyer (or near-qualified graduate) ready for your next career step in a firm that values people and purpose, we would love to hear from you.

Remuneration is competitive and negotiable for an exceptional candidate.

Apply now with your CV and Academic Transcript. Any questions direct to Georgia Robb at Profile Group - Georgia@profilegroup.co.nz

job.title: Senior Finance Business Partner
job.description:
The Opportunity
This is an opportunity for an experienced finance professional to step into a Senior Finance Business Partner role within a well-established manufacturing environment in Christchurch. Working closely with operational and commercial leaders, you will bring financial clarity to day-to-day decisions and help shape stronger business performance.

The role offers broad exposure across manufacturing operations, financial accounting, planning and commercial decision-making. You will combine robust analysis with strong financial discipline, helping lift core finance processes and controls to an audit-ready standard while turning financial and operational data into clear actions that support sustainable performance.

The Company
This is an established manufacturing business with a strong market presence and a clear focus on quality, operational performance and continuous improvement. With an experienced leadership team and a collaborative culture, the business offers a commercially focused environment where finance is closely connected to operations and decision-making.

The Role
You’ll be the go-to finance partner, responsible for:
  • Partnering with operational and commercial leaders to provide clear financial insight, challenge and decision support.
  • Leading budgeting, forecasting and business planning, including scenario modelling and regular performance reviews.
  • Delivering timely management reporting and explaining results against budget, forecast and prior periods.
  • Supporting month-end and year-end financial accounting, including balance sheet reconciliations, journals, accruals and reporting accuracy.
  • Strengthening financial controls, documentation and supporting schedules to lift finance processes to an audit-ready standard.
  • Coordinating audit requirements and responding to information requests, with clear ownership of issues through to resolution.
  • Analysing manufacturing performance, including margins, yields, labour, overheads, inventory and cost variances.
  • Identifying performance risks and opportunities, translating analysis into practical recommendations and measurable actions.
  • Supporting pricing, product, customer, investment and capital expenditure decisions through robust commercial analysis and business cases.
  • Improving reporting, planning and finance processes while strengthening financial understanding and accountability across the business.
  
Your Profile
You will bring:
  • CA qualification or an equivalent professional accounting designation.
  • Strong commercial finance experience, ideally gained within manufacturing, FMCG or another operationally complex environment.
  • Well-developed budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling and analytical capability.
  • Advanced spreadsheet skills, together with confidence using ERP and business reporting systems.
  • The ability to build credibility with non-finance stakeholders, ask constructive questions and influence commercial decisions.
  • A clear, practical communication style, with the ability to turn complex information into meaningful insight and action.
  • Sound financial accounting capability, with practical experience of reconciliations, controls, audit preparation and statutory reporting requirements.
  • A process improvement mindset, with the confidence to identify gaps, establish clear documentation and embed disciplined, repeatable finance processes.

job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
The Opportunity
Reporting to the MD, you will own group reporting, management accounting and financial controls across five operating entities spanning construction, civil works, land development, sawmilling and landscaping. This includes the group close, consolidation, management accounts, reconciliations, intercompany eliminations and reporting pack, with clear analysis for board and funder reporting.

Success will mean a timely, reliable close, stronger controls, clearer reporting and more consistent processes. In return, you will join a visible senior finance role with ongoing development and an intended pathway towards CFO, subject to performance and group growth.

You will lead a finance team, oversee project claims and job-costing support, improve cashflow visibility and work closely with operational leaders. You will also strengthen workflows, controls and reporting tools, using automation and AI where they can reduce manual effort and improve accuracy.

The Company
This privately held New Zealand group operates across construction, civil contracting, land development, sawmilling and landscaping. Its project-based environment makes claims, WIP, job costing and cash timing central to performance, with finance being strengthened to support continued growth.

The culture is practical, values-led and low ego. You will work closely with the CFO, operational leaders, banks and other stakeholders, with genuine scope to improve reporting, processes and capability across the group.

The Role
You’ll keep the group numbers reliable and make them useful to the people running the work. Key responsibilities include:
  • Own month-end for all group entities — journals, reconciliations, management accounts, fixed asset registers and depreciation — and prepare the reporting pack with variance analysis and commentary for the CFO’s review.
  • Own group reporting across every entity, including complete balance sheet reconciliations, intercompany eliminations and the schedules that feed board and funder reporting.
  • Own the group financial controls framework and policy, including consistent coding, GST treatment, RWT across entities, and control discipline on tax and intercompany processes.
  • Manage project claims and support job-costing reporting, including Procore and claim hygiene, and direct the work of the Senior Accounts Payable Assistant so claims go out on time and AR follow-up stays tight.
  • Support forecasting, cashflow visibility and financial analysis for the CFO and senior leaders, including rolling forecast inputs, scenario work and early escalation when cash, timing or accuracy is at risk.
  • Lead the small finance team day to day — the Senior Accounts Payable Assistant and the incoming Assistant / Management Accountant — including one-on-ones, priorities, recruitment, onboarding and development.
  • Improve finance workflows, templates, reporting tools and automation across the group, including where AI and better systems can reduce error, speed up close and lift capability outside finance.

Your Profile
This seat needs someone who can live in the detail and still lead. You’ll bring:
  • CA or CPA qualification, with seven or more years in finance including experience owning a full consolidation and close process — not only contributing to one.
  • Strong experience in a Xero-based environment, and a proven ability to prepare accurate financial analysis and reporting inputs that senior leaders will actually use.
  • Experience leading or mentoring, with the organisation and judgement to hold both the recon and the deadline. Clear, professional communication is essential.
  • Ideally, experience across multiple New Zealand entities and exposure to construction, contracting or other project-based businesses — customer claims, project reporting, WIP or job costing are a genuine advantage, and Procore experience is useful.
  • Personal style that matches the group: reliable and well organised, calm under pressure, high standards and low ego, proactive and solutions-focused, comfortable speaking up early, and strong enough EQ to work with site teams, the CFO and external stakeholders in the same week.

job.title: Project Accountant
job.description:
The Opportunity
You’re a project accountant who likes being useful - not just closing the books. You want a role where month-end still matters, but so does sitting with project managers, understanding what’s happening on their jobs, and explaining the numbers in plain language.

Based in Christchurch and reporting to the Finance Manager, you’ll look after the integrity of the financial accounts and help keep month-end accurate and on time. You’ll review journals, reconciliations and work prepared by others, support fixed assets, leases, GST, FBT and income tax, and play a visible part in year-end and audit. Just as important, you’ll build real working relationships with project managers - reviewing revenue, costs, accruals and margins, and helping them understand performance, risk and forecast outcomes rather than reporting the numbers after the fact.

Over the next 12 months a key part of the role is developing the finance team. Processes are being shared more widely, and you’ll train, coach and review others so the team has more depth and can operate with less reliance on any one person. If you enjoy lifting people as well as lifting the quality of the numbers, this is a role that will use both sides of how you work.

The Company
You’ll join a well-established Christchurch business that delivers solutions for clients across New Zealand. Work is project-based, so finance sits close to delivery - supporting project managers, keeping commercial information current, and helping the business see performance early enough to act. 

The Role
You’ll keep the accounts sound and make the numbers useful to the people delivering the work. Key responsibilities include:
  • Review project revenue, costs, accruals, margins and financial position; challenge unusual movements and help project managers understand the commercial story behind their results
  • Support project revenue recognition and month-end project accounting, and give practical financial advice to project managers and operational leader. 
  • Support an accurate, timely month-end close — maintain general ledger integrity, prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, journals, accruals and adjustments
  • Support accounting for fixed assets, depreciation, capital work in progress, leases and other month-end adjustments, and assist with GST, FBT, income tax, year-end reporting and external audit
  • Build trusted working relationships with project managers; join regular project financial reviews and develop a clear view of performance, risks, opportunities and forecast outcomes
  • (Once up to speed) Coach and train finance team members across accounting and month-end processes, review their work, explain the principles behind the tasks, and act as an escalation point for more complex transactions
Your Profile
Technical accounting ability matters here - but so does how you work with people. You’ll bring:
  • Ideally, strong financial or project accounting experience, a sound grasp of accounting principles, and proven month-end, reconciliation and general ledger review skills - including confidence reviewing the work of others
  • Excellent communication and relationship skills; you’re comfortable working with project managers and other non-finance stakeholders, and can explain accounting clearly without talking down. 
  • Strong Excel skills, confidence in financial systems (MYOB experience is useful), and the ability to manage competing priorities in a busy project environment
  • Ideally, experience in construction, engineering, infrastructure or another project-based industry, including long-term contracts, margins, variations and revenue recognition; CA/CPA (or working towards) is highly regarded
